About Upstart

At Upstart, we’re united by a mission that matters: to radically reduce the cost and complexity of borrowing for all Americans. Every day, we bring creativity, experimentation, and advanced AI to reshape access to credit, helping millions move forward financially with clarity and confidence.

As the leading AI lending marketplace, we partner with banks and credit unions to expand access to affordable credit through technology that’s both radically intelligent and deeply human. Our platform runs over one million predictions per borrower using more than 3,000 signals, powering smarter, fairer decisions for millions of customers. But the numbers only hint at the impact. Every idea, every voice, and every contribution moves us closer to a world where credit never stands between people and their financial progress.

We’re proudly digital-first, giving most Upstarters the flexibility to do their best work from wherever they thrive, alongside teammates across 80+ cities in the US and Canada. Digital-first doesn’t mean distant. We’re intentional about in-person connection through team onsites, planning sessions, and moments that spark creativity and trust. And whether you choose to work primarily from home or collaborate in-person from one of our offices in Columbus, Austin, the Bay Area, or New York City, you’ll have the support to work in the way that works best for you.

If you’re energized by tackling meaningful problems, excited to innovate with purpose, and motivated by work that truly matters, we’d love to hear from you.

The Team: 

Upstart is seeking a Recovery Vendor Performance Manager to drive the performance of our agency partners that provide post charge off collections services. You will own the oversight and outcomes of an assigned portfolio of recovery agencies across primary, secondary, tertiary, and debt settlement channels. By analyzing and managing vendor performance, you will help maximize recovery, ensure partners meet performance and compliance expectations, and deliver a personalized, seamless borrower experience while supporting appropriate borrower treatment.

Working with the Senior Operations Manager and Recovery team, you will manage control and compliance initiatives and connect vendor performance, quality, complaints, market share, audit oversight, and issue resolution to strong business outcomes.

This role requires independent ownership of strategic programs and the operating details that keep vendor commitments moving. You will validate information, communicate proactively, follow through on actions, and raise risks early.

How you’ll make an impact

  • Own an assigned portfolio of recovery agencies. Manage agency performance, quality, compliance, and day to day operations. Set clear expectations, identify root causes, document commitments, follow through with vendors and internal partners, and verify resolution.
  • Lead the vendor performance operating rhythm. Validate performance data and scorecards, prepare for and lead recurring weekly, monthly, and quarterly vendor reviews and listening sessions, and turn results into actions with clear owners and timelines. Use relevant measures such as liquidation, payer activity, contact rates, settlement outcomes, quality, and service levels.
  • Develop performance based market share recommendations. Evaluate weighted liquidation results alongside quality, compliance, remediation, risk, and capacity signals. Prepare quarterly allocation recommendations for Recovery leadership, coordinate approved changes, and confirm that placements reflect decisions. Distinguish strategic market share decisions from routine account rotation.
  • Own vendor audit and compliance oversight programs. Coordinate audit planning, evidence review, vendor communication, findings, corrective action plans, remediation tracking, and closure verification with Compliance, Quality, Audit, TPRM, and Recovery partners. Coordinate annual onsite reviews of vendor controls and operational performance. Validate whether findings reflect agency gaps or internal process gaps, route them to the right owners, and track them through resolution.
  • Oversee complaints and borrower protection. Monitor complaint reporting and data quality, identify trends and potential risk, obtain vendor responses, track corrective actions, and escalate material or recurring concerns. Monitor adherence to applicable borrower protections and requirements, and coordinate corrective action when issues arise.
  • Resolve vendor and internal process issues. Partner with agencies, the Settlements team, and internal owners to investigate settlement errors, payment or balance discrepancies, and other operational issues. Clarify ownership, drive corrective actions, and confirm agreed process changes are implemented.
  • Manage SLAs and  contractual expectations and remediation. Monitor vendor performance against applicable service levels and contractual requirements. Validate issues, document supporting evidence, assign owners and due dates, and escalate unresolved or repeat concerns.
  • Strengthen the oversight operating model. Build and maintain scalable vendor procedures, controls, performance measures, and data standards. Use analytics, reporting, and responsible AI or automation to improve the accuracy, consistency, and efficiency of oversight. Identify internal process or data gaps that affect vendor outcomes and partner with the right teams to address them.
  • Communicate and follow through reliably. Maintain an organized calendar and accurate recurring deliverables. Respond to vendors and internal partners in a timely manner, provide proactive status updates, track commitments to closure, and escalate risks or blockers early.
  • Support vendor engagement. Build constructive agency relationships, support vendor recognition activities, and collaborate with Recovery, Settlements, Legal, Compliance, Quality, Risk, TPRM, Product, and Engineering partners.
  • Travel for vendor oversight. Coordinate and attend agency onsite reviews and related meetings. Travel is a recurring part of the role and may occur nearly monthly.

 

Minimum Qualifications 

  • 5+ years of experience in collections and recovery, preferably in fintech or financial services.
  • 5+ years of experience managing external vendors or agency relationships and holding partners accountable to measurable outcomes.
  • Demonstrated ability to own complex work from issue identification through verified resolution, including proactive communication and dependable follow through.
  • Demonstrated ability to drive business outcomes and improve customer experiences through vendor relationships.
  • Strong analytical skills, including the ability to validate performance data, identify trends, and translate findings into decisions and actions.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication and negotiation skills, with the ability to influence vendor partners and internal stakeholders.
  • Strong organization and calendar management skills.
  • Ability to thrive in a fast paced, high growth environment with a strong sense of urgency.
  • Knowledge of collections compliance and regulatory expectations in financial services.
  • Ability to travel for agency onsite reviews and vendor meetings, with travel occurring nearly monthly.

Preferred Qualifications 

  • Experience building collections, vendor procedures, performance measures, or control metrics from the ground up.
  • Experience managing legal agencies, including pre-legal and state-level attorney performance and compliance.
  • Practical experience using AI tools or automation to improve analysis, reporting, or operational workflows, with sound judgment around accuracy, confidentiality, and data handling.
  • Experience leading vendor audit, complaint oversight, remediation, or corrective action programs.
  • Experience supporting vendor onsite reviews and presenting performance or risk findings to leadership.

 

Position location This role is available in the following locations: Remote . 

Travel requirements As a digital first company, the majority of your work can be accomplished remotely. The majority of our employees can live and work anywhere in the U.S but are encouraged to to still spend high quality time in-person collaborating via regular onsites. The in-person sessions’ cadence varies depending on the team and role; most teams meet once or twice per quarter for 2-4 consecutive days at a time.

The Recovery organization also coordinates vendor travel across the team. This role will coordinate and participate in agency onsite reviews as assigned. Vendor travel cadence varies by role and business needs, and travel across Recovery may occur nearly monthly.

#LI-REMOTE

#LI-Associate 

At Upstart, your base pay is one part of your total compensation package.  The anticipated base salary for this position is expected to be within the below range. Your actual base pay will depend on your geographic location–with our “digital first” philosophy, Upstart uses compensation regions that vary depending on location. Individual pay is also determined by job-related skills, experience, and relevant education or training. Your recruiter can share more about the specific salary range for your preferred location during the hiring process.

In addition, Upstart provides employees with target bonuses, equity compensation, and generous benefits packages (including medical, dental, vision, and 401k).

United States | Remote - Anticipated Base Salary Range
$79,000—$109,200 USD

What you'll love

At Upstart, our benefits for full-time employees are designed to support your health, financial well-being, family, and personal growth. Here’s what you can expect:

  • Competitive compensation, including base pay, bonus opportunities, and annual equity grants that vest quarterly 
  • Retirement benefits to help you plan for the future, including a 401(k) or Group Retirement Savings Plan with a company match of $2 for every $1 contributed, up to $15,000 annually (USD in the US, CAD in Canada)
  • Employee Stock Purchase Plan (ESPP) with discounted stock purchase options for eligible employees (US only)
  • Comprehensive health coverage designed to support you and your family, including medical, dental, vision, and wellness resources for US and supplemental health coverage for Canada.
  • Health Savings Account contributions from Upstart for eligible plans (US only)
  • Income protection benefits, including life insurance and disability coverage for added financial security
  • Paid time off, sick leave, and company holidays, in line with local requirements
  • Paid family and parental leave to support caregiving and major life moments (duration varies by country)
  • Family-centered benefits to support fertility, parenthood, and caregiving needs
  • Employee Assistance Program (EAP) offering mental health support and life-centered resources
  • Financial wellness resources, including access to financial planning tools and a financial concierge service (US Only)
  • Annual wellness allowance to support your physical and emotional well-being and personal development, based on what matters most to you
  • Annual productivity allowance to invest in relevant tools and resources you need to do your best work, no matter where you work from
  • Connection and community through team events, all-company updates, and employee resource groups (ERGs)
  • Onsite perks, including catered lunches and fully stocked micro-kitchens when working from one of our offices in the Bay Area, Austin, Columbus, and New York City

For roles based in Canada, please note that we are not currently able to hire in Quebec.

Upstart is a proud Equal Opportunity Employer. Just as we are dedicated to improving access to affordable credit for all, we are committed to inclusive and fair hiring practices.

If you require reasonable accommodation in completing an application, interviewing, completing any pre-employment testing, or otherwise participating in the employee selection process, please email candidate_accommodations@upstart.com
